survivors_flagged.one_line: All-stock Black Hills merger (Bright Horizon): FERC, Nebraska and South Dakota approved; the Montana PSC order (docket 2025.10.078) is the last gate, with close guided by YE2026. Fixed ratio, so the spread is likely thin.

verified.catalyst: The all-stock Black Hills merger (fixed 0.98 BKH per NWE share, combined company to be named Bright Horizon Energy) is waiting only on a final order from the Montana PSC, with close guided by year-end 2026.
verified.dated_milestone: The Montana PSC final order has no statutory deadline. The hearing was held in May 2026. In September 2026 the PSC voted that Commissioner Bushman may take part in the decision, and that question is still being challenged in Lewis and Clark County District Court. Next date: an MPSC vote, expected by about Q4 2026, then close by YE2026.
verified.instrument: Long NWE / short 0.98x BKH (spread trade). An outright long NWE is just a BKH/utility beta bet.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 (named counterparty Black Hills) and G2 (signed merger agreement with a fixed 0.98 ratio; FERC, Nebraska, South Dakota, HSR and shareholder approvals done) both pass. G3 fails: the spread is about 0.5%, so no meaningful unpriced figure remains.
verified.edge: L. On 2026-10-12, 0.98 x BKH $76.08 = $74.56 implied, against NWE at $74.15, a gross spread of about 0.55%. Quarterly dividends are roughly equal per share, so they add or remove almost nothing. That works out to about 2-3% annualized over a 2-3 month close, which is below T-bills. Run-up: NWE was about $57 before the August 2025 announcement (52-week low $57.12) and is now $74.15, roughly +30%. Most of that is the BKH/utility rally, since the deal premium was only about 4%. Remaining: about +0.5% to the deal value. Downside if Montana blocks the deal: NWE falls back to standalone value, likely several % below today, which is very asymmetric against a 0.5% gain. Mostly harvested.
verified.primary_source: FMP batch-quote NWE $74.15 / BKH $76.08 (2026-10-12); NWE Q2-2026 10-Q and earnings release (2026-07-29): Montana is the only approval left, close expected by YE2026; Black Hills 8-K (Aug 2025): 0.98 exchange ratio; Daily Montanan / States Newsroom (Sep 2026): MPSC procedural vote on Commissioner Bushman and the pending court challenge.
verified.analysis: The event is real, dated and forward: Montana is the only approval left, a settlement with key intervenors is pending before the MPSC, and close is guided by YE2026. But at a fixed ratio the market prices NWE within about 0.55% of 0.98 x BKH, so almost all of the value is already captured. A Montana denial or tough conditions (and the court challenge over Commissioner Bushman's vote could slow things) carries far more downside than the remaining spread offers. Gap: I could not confirm whether the MPSC issued an order after the September procedural vote. Check docket 2025.10.078 directly.
